page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ESv4 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with a memory capacity of 504.0 GB, yielding 31.5 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations position the E64-16s_v4 in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The single-core stress-ng performance score is 1573.9, and the multi-core score is 12871.56. Memory bandwidth tests show 695.21 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 99.79 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, certain workloads show performance tradeoffs; single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak at 8.55 GB/sec, and LLM inference speeds for a 7B model are limited to 24.55 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 7.79 tokens/sec for text generation.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require proportional CPU scaling. It is well-suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications. The lack of local storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for local high-speed scratch disk operations or heavy parallel graphics processing, but its dedicated CPU allocation and high RAM density support stable database operations and memory-intensive enterprise tasks.
